title: GOAL SETTING
mv: The plans of the diligent lead surely to plenty, But those of everyone who is hasty, surely to poverty.
mvp: “The plans of the diligent lead surely to plenty, But those of everyone who is hasty, surely to poverty.” Proverbs 21:5 (NKJV)
assignment: Do a breakdown of your Career goal into five-year, one-year, six-month, one-month and one-week goal (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: A goal is a desirable outcome that someone carefully decides on, commits to, and plans to attain. Goal setting is the deliberate act of identifying what you want to achieve and planning on how to accomplish it. God created humans with purpose, direction, and the ability to plan. Without clear goals, life becomes disorganised, unproductive, and unclear (Proverbs 29:18). Setting godly goals helps believers maximise time, develop discipline, and ultimately fulfil God’s will.
Areas where we can set goals include:

i: Career: Decide what level you want to reach in your career, or what you want to achieve. (Proverbs 11:23; 23:18).
Finance: Set a goal for your earnings (Proverbs 21:5).
Education: Set academic goals in line with your career (Proverbs 2:3).
Family: What kind of relationship/partner do you want? How many children do you want? How do you want to be seen by a partner or in-laws? (Proverbs 18:24; 2 Corinthians 6:14).
Attitude: Do you have character defects or anything in your mindset holding you back? If so, set a goal to improve your behaviour or find a solution to the problem (Matthew 7:17-20).
Physical: Are there physical fitness goals you want to achieve now and later in life? What steps are you taking to achieve this? (1 Timothy 4:8a).
Pleasure: How do you want to enjoy yourself after you have worked? What plans do you have for vacation? Spend time to celebrate yourself (Ecclesiastes 5:18).
Public Service: Do you want to make the world a better place? If so, how? (Matthew 5:14).

b.x: Believers must seek God’s guidance before setting goals, (Acts 9:6). Prayer ensures that goals are Spirit-inspired, not self-driven. A good understanding of one’s strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and spiritual needs will also be of help. Large goals may be overwhelming; break them into small, manageable tasks. For example, a goal to read the Bible in a year requires a daily plan. Small steps build momentum and lead to long-term success (Zechariah 4:10a). Share your goals with trusted mentors, friends, or spiritual leaders who can motivate you, correct you, and check your progress. Regular assessment is essential; review your goals weekly or monthly, adjust when necessary and celebrate victories whether big or small. Gratitude keeps you motivated and strengthens your faith.

A useful way to actualise your goals is to adopt the SMART acronym; ensure your goal is Specific (Habakkuk 2:2-3), Measurable (Luke 14:28), Attainable (Proverbs 16:3), Realistic (Proverbs 21:5), and Time-bound (Ecclesiastes 3:17b) as these aids the actualisation.
Set meaningful and achievable goals to fulfil destiny.
